channel.title: Brazil Elections 2026
channel.description: Real-time monitoring of the 2026 Brazilian presidential elections.

item.title: Queda da fila do INSS acelera nos últimos meses; benefícios negados sobem e chegam a quase 1 milhão em junho
item.description: The INSS benefit waiting list dropped to 1.55 million in July, the lowest level in 21 months, with a 74% reduction year-to-date. However, benefit denials surged, nearing 1 million in June and rising 70% compared to the same period last year, particularly for disability-related benefits. Experts warn this approach may merely shift demand to judicialization, as many denied claims could lead to new applications, administrative appeals, or court actions.

item.title: Assassinatos de indígenas aumentam durante governo Lula
item.description: Indigenous killings in Brazil rose in 2025 for the third consecutive year, according to a report by the Indigenist Missionary Council (Cimi), linked to the Catholic Church. The increase occurred during the government of President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, despite his promises to protect Indigenous peoples.

item.title: Petrobras encontra sinais de petróleo na bacia da Foz do Amazonas - por que projeto de exploração ali é controverso?
item.description: Petrobras has found indications of oil in the Foz do Amazonas basin, in ultra-deep waters off Amapá, though economic viability remains unconfirmed. The project is controversial due to the region's ecological sensitivity and opposition from environmental groups, despite support from the Lula government and Petrobras's claims of technological safety and energy demand fulfillment.

item.title: Governador do MA diz estar sendo julgado por um adversário político
item.description: Maranhão Governor Carlos Brandão (MDB) challenged Minister Flávio Dino's STF decision lifting secrecy on PF investigations into corruption, embezzlement, witness intimidation, and obstruction of justice involving state political leaders, arguing the STF lacks jurisdiction over governors and that he is being politically targeted by an adversary ahead of the 2026 elections. He also criticized the investigation's temporal focus, claiming it omits the 2019 reopening of a 2014 administrative payment process for R$ 800 million owed to SH Vigilância — allegedly the true motive behind the 2022 killing of João Bosco Sobrinho Pereira de Oliveira.

item.title: Bolsonaro pede a Moraes para ir a dentista e indica mulher de Flávio
item.description: Jair Bolsonaro's defense requested authorization from Supreme Court Minister Alexandre de Moraes for the former president to attend a dental appointment on August 21 at 2:00 p.m. at the Terracota Clinical Center in Brasília. The dentist named is Fernanda Antunes Figueira Bolsonaro, wife of Senator and presidential candidate Flávio Bolsonaro. The request comes despite a 30-day visitation ban, with exceptions for health professionals, and follows Moraes’ restriction on political visits after Bolsonaro published a letter endorsing Flávio as his 'spokesperson' in the presidential race.

item.title: Bolsonaro pede ao STF autorização para ir a consulta odontológica com mulher de Flávio
item.description: Former President Jair Bolsonaro has requested authorization from the STF to temporarily leave house arrest for a dental appointment next Friday. The dentist indicated by his defense is Fernanda Antunes Figueira Bolsonaro, wife of his son Flávio Bolsonaro, who is currently barred from visiting him under a 90-day restriction ordered by Minister Alexandre de Moraes. The defense argues the leave would be strictly for the appointment, subject to relevant monitoring measures.

item.title: TSE remarca reunião sobre IA de Bolsonaro para 3ª feira
item.description: The Superior Electoral Court (TSE) has rescheduled a private meeting for Tuesday, August 18, 2026, to discuss whether an AI-generated video of Jair Bolsonaro constitutes a prohibited deepfake under Resolution 23.732/2024. Minister Nunes Marques aims to establish a precedent on AI use in electoral campaigns, as the PT claims the video, used during Flávio Bolsonaro’s convention, violates electoral rules despite being positive in tone. The case is also under review by the Supreme Federal Court (STF) following allegations of judicial non-compliance by Bolsonaro.

item.title: Bolsonaro pede ao STF para ir à dentista e indica esposa de Flávio para atendimento
item.description: Former President Jair Bolsonaro requested STF authorization to leave house arrest for a dental appointment, naming his daughter-in-law Fernanda Antunes Figueira Bolsonaro — wife of Senator Flávio Bolsonaro — as his treating dentist. The appointment is scheduled for March 21 at 2:00 p.m. Bolsonaro is serving house arrest following a conviction for a coup plot and is recovering from bacterial pneumonia.

item.title: Flávio é o candidato mais rejeitado, aponta Quaest
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) is the most rejected presidential candidate according to a Quaest poll released on March 14, with 54% of respondents rejecting him. He is followed by President Lula (PT) at 52% rejection and former governor Ronaldo Caiado (PSD) at 35%. The poll also lists former governor Romeu Zema as the next in line.

item.title: ‘Eles articularam’: Marina Silva responsabiliza família Bolsonaro pelo tarifaço
item.description: Marina Silva, the Rede Sustentabilidade candidate for the Senate from São Paulo, stated that the U.S. tariff hike harms strategic sectors of São Paulo's economy, including footwear, auto parts, coffee, and biofuels, and attributed it to the Bolsonaro family's articulation, which, she said, fails to separate political interests from national strategic interests. She also criticized Governor Tarcísio de Freitas for not joining the Propag program, which she said caused a loss of nearly R$ 11 billion, and argued that Brazil cannot accept economic losses driven by political interests.

item.title: Kassab reafirma que Flávio não vence eleição e diz que centrão favorece PT
item.description: Gilberto Kassab, president of the PSD and running mate of Ronaldo Caiado, reaffirmed that Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) will not win the 2026 presidential election and stated that centrist leaders support Lula's (PT) reelection. His remarks highlight internal fractures on the right and suggest a broad coalition forming around the current government.

item.title: Novas imagens mostram aproximação da PM a motorista de Haddad
item.description: New images released by São Paulo's SSP show a police cruiser slowly passing by the car of Fernando Haddad's driver on Joinville Street, but they do not confirm any interaction or approach. The SSP reiterated there is no evidence of irregular procedure, after analyzing over 40 security cameras and vehicle geolocation data. The incident has intensified campaign tensions, with Haddad suggesting political persecution by his rival, Tarcísio de Freitas.

item.title: TSE e USP testam urna eletrônica mais acessível
item.description: The TSE and USP are testing a more accessible electronic voting machine, with interface changes to improve usability, especially for people with disabilities. The project involves LARC from the Polytechnic School and FAU, aiming to adapt the equipment for the 2026 general elections.

item.title: Quaest: Edinho minimiza empate técnico entre Lula e Flávio no 2º turno
item.description: Edinho Silva, national president of the Workers' Party (PT), downplayed the technical tie between Lula (43%) and Flávio Bolsonaro (40%) in a potential second round, according to a Quaest poll, stating that polls are 'snapshots of the moment' and that the PT's campaign focus begins only on August 16, the official start of the 2026 election campaign. He emphasized that the governing base is not concerned with isolated numbers but with future trends.

item.title: Ronaldo Caiado declara R$ 52,5 milhões em bens; Kassab informa R$ 21 milhões
item.description: Ronaldo Caiado declared R$ 52.5 million in assets to the Electoral Justice, an increase of 111% from the R$ 25 million declared in 2022. Gilberto Kassab, the vice-presidential candidate on the PSD ticket, reported assets of R$ 21 million. Together, the two candidates declare a total of R$ 73.5 million in assets.

item.title: Haddad ataca ensino "decadente" e atribui taxa da blusinha a Tarcísio
item.description: Fernando Haddad criticized the decline of high school education in São Paulo under Tarcísio de Freitas' administration, citing failed pedagogical policies, lack of competitive hiring for teachers, deficient infrastructure in ETECs and FATECs, and lack of broadband in a third of schools. He also attributed the origin of the 'blusinha tax' to Tarcísio, denying it was started by João Doria and claiming the current governor lied about his responsibility for imposing ICMS on postal shipments.

item.title: O que Tarcísio tem a ver com liberação de 13 bi em empréstimos do governo Lula a cinco estados
item.description: The Lula government released nearly 13 billion reais in loans to five states — São Paulo, Rondônia, Piauí, Pernambuco, and Maranhão — to counter claims that it was withholding funds to benefit Fernando Haddad in the 2026 elections. The move followed accusations by Governor Tarcísio de Freitas that the Ministry of Finance was deliberately delaying a 5.4 billion reais disbursement to harm him electorally. Finance Minister Dario Durigan signed the credit operations, stating the process was proceeding normally and the release was expected.

item.title: Lula vai usar descoberta de petróleo na Foz do Amazonas como aposta do mote ‘Brasil pronto pra mais’
item.description: Lula plans to use the oil discovery in the Amazon Foz, announced by Petrobras, as an electoral legacy under the slogan 'Brazil ready for more'. The discovery in the Equatorial Margin will be featured in TV, radio, and social media ads of the PT campaign, with the official launch this Sunday in São Bernardo do Campo. The move revives the 2008 symbolism when Lula stained his hands with pre-salt oil, reinforcing a narrative of energy continuity and political succession.

item.title: Alessandro Vieira: ‘Alguns’ ministros do STF podem ser alvo de impeachment
item.description: Senator Alessandro Vieira (MDB-SE) stated there are 'strong indications of responsibility crime' involving three Supreme Court ministers — Dias Toffoli, Alexandre de Moraes, and Gilmar Mendes — and argued that, after due process, some could face impeachment. He denied using the STF confrontation as an electoral strategy, emphasizing his re-election campaign should focus on accountability. Vieira also endorsed Ronaldo Caiado in the first round of the presidential election and commented on the progress of the Public Security PEC and the 6×1 workweek reform.

item.title: 'É uma eleição de quem é menos rejeitado': como os colunistas do GLOBO avaliam a nova pesquisa Quaest; assista
item.description: The Quaest poll commissioned by TV Globo and O GLOBO shows Lula at 38% and Flávio Bolsonaro at 31% in the first round, indicating a technical tie in the second round. Globo columnists argue the 2026 election will be decided by who is less rejected, with Lula having a 'glass roof' and bolsonarism remaining alive due to rejection of the PT, not Flávio's strength.

item.title: João Campos vai à cidade natal de Lula em ato simbólico de campanha
item.description: Former Recife mayor João Campos (PSB), candidate for governor of Pernambuco in 2026, announced he will launch his campaign symbolically in Caetés, President Lula’s birthplace, on Saturday, August 15, one day before official electoral campaigning begins. The visit follows a recording session with Lula in Brasília, and Campos emphasized the president’s public and solidified support for his candidacy. He also confirmed Lula will visit Pernambuco during the campaign as part of a broader Northeastern regional itinerary, underscoring the personal and political significance of the state in Lula’s life.

item.title: Site do Missão oferece “filiação oficial” no TSE
item.description: The Missão party’s website offers ‘official’ affiliation via paid plans, but the process raises fraud concerns after Senator Flávio Bolsonaro appeared as a member without his consent. The party denounced a fraudulent affiliation attempt, and the TSE’s affiliation system was suspended for security reasons, while Flávio’s campaign confirmed his return to the PL and the launch of his presidential bid.

item.title: Quaest: campanha de Flávio vê nova fase e aposta em propostas, enquanto PT prepara ofensiva
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro's (PL) campaign celebrated the narrowing gap with Lula (PT) in the Quaest poll, which dropped from eight to three points in the second round — within the margin of error. Campaign allies say the official start of electoral advertising marks a 'new phase,' shifting focus from reactive messaging to policy proposals, with Gaspar's vice-presidential pick aimed at boosting Northeastern support. While optimistic about a technical tie, some party members question Gaspar's ability to convert visibility into votes.

item.title: Bolsonaro pede autorização para ida ao dentista
item.description: Former President Jair Bolsonaro requested permission from Minister Alexandre de Moraes of the Supreme Federal Court to temporarily leave house arrest for a dental appointment next Friday, the 21st, at 2 p.m. The dentist selected by his defense is Fernanda Antunes Figueira Bolsonaro, wife of Senator Flávio Bolsonaro. The request was submitted through his legal team.

item.title: Petistas atribuem más notícias da Quaest a Jaques, Lulinha e Marcola
item.description: PT leaders attribute the drop in Lula's lead over Flávio Bolsonaro from five to three points in the Quaest poll to negative news involving Jaques Wagner, Lulinha, and Marcola over the past 30 days. Despite the decline, Lula's allies do not view the situation as definitive and expect a recovery with the start of the campaign. They hope new developments in the Master Case could benefit Lula.

item.title: Quaest: Flávio amplia vantagem entre eleitores da direita não bolsonarista
item.description: Quaest poll shows Senator Flávio Bolsonaro increased his lead among non-bolsonarist right-wing voters, rising from 66% to 70% in voting intentions. Former Goiás governor Ronaldo Caiado came in second with 6%, followed by Lula (PT) and other unspecified candidates. The result reflects Flávio’s growing consolidation of support within this moderate right-wing electorate.

item.title: Flávio diz que Kassab “entregou o jogo” e associa PSD a Lula
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) accused Gilberto Kassab, president of the PSD and vice-presidential candidate on Ronaldo Caiado's ticket, of having 'given away the game' by claiming the PSD is effectively aligned with Lula. He stated his candidacy is the only truly right-wing option, aiming to 'rescue Brazil from captivity,' not for power. Campaign coordinator Senator Rogério Marinho added that the PSD has three ministers in Lula's government and acts as an auxiliary line for the PT.

item.title: Nem Michelle, nem Bia: Prudente anuncia apoio à candidatura de Sebastião Coelho
item.description: Federal deputy Rafael Prudente (MDB) announced his support for Sebastião Coelho (Novo) as Senate candidate in the Federal District, breaking with the MDB’s formal alliance with Governor Celina Leão (PP), whose slate includes Michelle Bolsonaro and Bia Kicis for Senate. Prudente stated his support for Coelho is clear and expressed confidence in a strong alliance and joint campaign. Coelho, a retired TJDFT judge, said he received the news with great joy, emphasizing their shared mission for Brazil and the DF.

item.title: Defesa de Bolsonaro pede autorização para ex-presidente deixar a prisão domiciliar e ir ao dentista
item.description: Bolsonaro's defense requested authorization from Minister Alexandre de Moraes of the STF for the former president to temporarily leave house arrest and visit a dentist on the 21st of this month. Bolsonaro is under house arrest for humanitarian reasons, serving a 27-year-and-three-month sentence for involvement in a coup plot, and requires judicial approval for any departure from his residence. The dental appointment will be conducted by Fernanda Antunes Figueira Bolsonaro, wife of Flávio Bolsonaro.

item.title: Crusoé: Renan alcança 10% entre os jovens no primeiro turno, aponta pesquisa
item.description: Renan Santos, candidate of the Mission to the Presidency, reached 10% voting intention among voters aged 16 to 32, according to the Genial/Quaest poll. However, his performance is weak among voters over 34, with only 1% in the 35–59 and 60+ age brackets, indicating strong youth appeal but limited traction with older voters.

item.title: Quaest: violência é a principal preocupação dos eleitores em todas as regiões do país
item.description: The Quaest poll shows violence as the top concern for voters across all Brazilian regions, cited by 33% of respondents, peaking at 39% in the Northeast and among low-income earners. Lula leads first-round voting intentions at 38%, followed by Flávio Bolsonaro at 31%, while in a potential runoff Lula reaches 43% and Flávio 40%. Economy, health, and corruption follow as secondary concerns at 15%, 14%, and 14%.

item.title: Por Dentro das Eleições: saiba os ilícitos eleitorais e as condutas vedadas a agentes públicos
item.description: Brazilian electoral legislation establishes strict rules to ensure the fairness of elections, prohibiting general electoral offenses and specific conducts forbidden to public agents during the so-called 'electoral blackout period'. The norms, consolidated by Resolution No. 23.735/2024 and amended by Resolution No. 23.757/2026, cover everything from prohibitions for public servants to the most serious violations that affect vote authenticity and equal opportunity among candidates.

item.title: Quaest: 45% dizem que temem mais a volta dos Bolsonaro; 41% afirmam que é a permanência de Lula
item.description: The Quaest poll shows 45% of voters fear the return of the Bolsonaro family to power, while 41% fear a new Lula term. 6% fear both scenarios and 3% fear neither. 5% did not know or did not respond.

item.title: Com Flávio no cangote, Lula tenta aprovar fim da 6x1 antes da eleição
item.description: Lula leads the 2026 presidential race with 38% in the first round, but Flávio Bolsonaro has narrowed the gap to 7 points, standing at 31%. In a hypothetical runoff, Lula's advantage shrinks to 3 points (43% to 40%), resulting in a technical tie within the margin of error.

item.title: Quaest: 56% acham que Lula será reeleito presidente; 27% acreditam em vitória de Flávio
item.description: A Quaest poll, commissioned by O Globo and TV Globo, shows that 56% of voters believe President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) will be re-elected in October, while 27% expect Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) to win. Released on Friday, the 14th, the survey reflects voter perceptions of the 2026 electoral landscape.

item.title: Quaest: No Sudeste, em segundo turno, Flávio tem 44% e Lula, 36% das intenções de voto
item.description: A Quaest poll, released by O Globo and TV Globo, shows that in a hypothetical second-round scenario in the Southeast region, Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) leads with 44% of voting intentions, while President Lula trails at 36%. The Southeast region concentrates 66.6 million voters, equivalent to 42% of the Brazilian electorate.

item.title: Rogério Marinho rebate Kassab e diz que candidatura de Caiado 'não é para valer'
item.description: Senator Rogério Marinho (PL-RN), coordinator of Flávio Bolsonaro's (PL) presidential campaign, rebuked a statement by PSD president Gilberto Kassab, asserting that Ronaldo Caiado's (PSD) candidacy 'is not for real'. He questioned the viability of Caiado's candidacy as an alternative to the Bolsonarist camp.

item.title: Bolsonaro pede a Moraes para ir à dentista: a nora, mulher de Flávio
item.description: Jair Bolsonaro requested permission from Supreme Court Justice Alexandre de Moraes to temporarily leave his house arrest for a dental appointment with Fernanda Bolsonaro, wife of his son Flávio, at a clinic in Lago Sul, Brasília, on August 21 at 2:00 PM. The request seeks authorization for the necessary time to travel, attend, and return, under appropriate supervision. This would be his first leave since being hospitalized for bronchopneumonia, while he remains barred from contacting Flávio until mid-October due to a prior violation of a court order regarding public support for his presidential candidacy.

item.title: Caiado propõe fim da reeleição e combate a “terrorismo doméstico”
item.description: Ronaldo Caiado (PSD), former governor of Goiás and 2026 presidential candidate, unveiled his government plan emphasizing fiscal adjustment, organized crime combat, and political reform — including ending consecutive re-election for executive offices and adopting a mixed-district electoral system. The plan also proposes a 'Truth Budget,' control of supersalaries, raising investment to 25% of GDP, and prioritizing security, education, health, and the environment.

item.title: Lula grava vídeo de campanha em apoio a senador alvo de investigação na fraude do INSS
item.description: President Lula recorded a campaign video in support of Senator Weverton Rocha (PDT-MA), who is seeking re-election, despite recent revelations that Supreme Court Minister Flávio Dino pointed to 'undue interference' by the senator in a murder case in Maranhão and that Weverton is under Federal Police investigation for INSS fraud. The senator defended his integrity, stating that Lula is not concerned about potential backlash, as he knows Weverton’s work in Congress.

item.title: Janones diz que Flávio domina redes e ultrapassará Lula em setembro
item.description: Federal deputy André Janones (Rede-MG) claimed that Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) will surpass President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) in polls by the second week of September, arguing that dominance in social media determines political outcomes. He criticized the left's communication strategy as outdated and emotional, asserting that analysts, commentators, and even Bolsonarists fail to grasp the coming shift.

item.title: Lula busca conversa com Trump e quer cobrar não interferência nas eleições
item.description: President Lula (PT) said he is trying to maintain contact with U.S. President Donald Trump to have a tête-à-tête conversation, in which he will ask Trump not to interfere in Brazilian elections. Lula stated he has never interfered in U.S. elections and questioned whether Trump would do the same in Brazil. Despite trade tensions, Lula aims to preserve dialogue with Washington, viewing Trump as more open than other U.S. officials like Marco Rubio.

item.title: “Quaest mostra uma eleição ainda polarizada, mas não totalmente decidida”
item.description: The Genial/Quaest poll released this Friday shows President Lula (PT) leading Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) by three percentage points in a hypothetical 2026 runoff scenario. Felipe Nunes, director of Genial/Quaest, commented on the result on X, noting that while the election remains polarized, it is not yet decided. The survey reflects a tight race with room for change before the election.

item.title: Quaest: Flávio Bolsonaro abre vantagem sobre Lula no Sudeste
item.description: The Quaest poll shows Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) gaining an advantage over Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) in the Southeast region, with 44% versus 36%, signaling a recovery following controversies involving his conversations with Daniel Vorcaro. In the national second-round scenario, Lula leads with 43% to Flávio’s 40%, within the margin of error, indicating a technical tie. The survey interviewed 2,004 voters from Monday to Thursday, with a two-point margin of error and 95% confidence level.

item.title: Quaest: Lula lidera no Nordeste e entre católicos; Flávio Bolsonaro, no Sul e entre evangélicos
item.description: Lula leads Flávio Bolsonaro in the electoral landscape, with his advantage rooted in the Northeast, among voters earning up to two minimum wages, Black individuals, those with up to elementary education, and Catholics. The Quaest poll shows Lula maintaining a lead over the senator, highlighting regional and socioeconomic divisions in the Brazilian electorate. The content is exclusive to subscribers.

item.title: Mulheres articulam agenda suprapartidária para as eleições na Alesp
item.description: The 'Women Who Think Brazil' project presented the Women's Charter for Politics at the Alesp on August 12, 2026, gathering leaders from public, private, judicial, and civil society sectors to discuss proposals on parity, governance, ESG, combating gender-based political violence, and economic development ahead of the 2026 elections. Initiated by electoral lawyer Gabriela Rollemberg, the event featured Simone Tebet, PSB Senate candidate, and other prominent figures, emphasizing its suprapartisan nature.

item.title: Quaest: Flávio (PL) é rejeitado por 54% dos eleitores; rejeição a Lula (PT) soma 52%
item.description: Quaest poll shows Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) has 54% rejection and President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) has 52%, making them the most rejected presidential candidates for 2026. The survey was released on Friday, March 14.

item.title: Quaest: Em pesquisa espontânea, Lula tem 25% e Flávio, 19%; 51% estão indecisos
item.description: In a spontaneous poll by Quaest, President Lula (PT) leads with 25% voting intentions, followed by Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) with 19%. A majority of voters, 51%, remain undecided, indicating a still-fluid landscape for the 2026 elections.

item.title: Quaest: Governo Lula é avaliado negativamente por 37%, positivamente por 36% e regular para 25%
item.description: President Lula’s government is viewed with near-equal division: 37% of voters rate it negatively, 36% positively, and 25% as regular, according to a Quaest poll released on March 14. The slim 1-point gap between positive and negative ratings reflects deep polarization. Only 2% were undecided or did not respond.

item.title: Quaest mostra Lula mais vulnerável na eleição, com piora na avaliação do governo
item.description: The Quaest poll shows President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva is more vulnerable in the 2026 election, with declining vote intention in a potential runoff and a technical tie solidified with Flávio Bolsonaro. Additionally, there is a significant deterioration in government approval, reflecting declining public confidence in the current administration.
